findings.problem: The hint contains the Spanish answer itself (fuera de), so the learner reads the answer instead of recalling it.
findings.fix: hint: as in out of town, followed by de; the shorter word, not afuera

back.es: out, outside (adverb); fuera de = out of, outside of
back.example: My dad is out of the city / out of town.

note: In Latin America afuera is more common than fuera for outside on its own, so the hint does need to rule afuera out and point to the fuera de construction.
